items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1978-Fall Transcript
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Ball Head' as the title of a song he recorded ('Ball Head was one in Mardi Gras, New Orleans'), but provides no information about a personal relationship with a person named Ball Head.

ctx.x: Yeah, they're rough. I'm going to ask you about one song. And you don't have to answer this if you don't feel like it. Somebody wanted me to ask you this. Is Ball of the Wall a dance? Does it mean something else? How did you come up with that?

The people came up with that. Since they've been calling Ball of the Wall, I've been trying to memorize myself where it really is. I don't remember no song I ever made by the name of Ball of the Wall, but I might have said Ball of the Wall in some of the things I was doing. And they took it for granted that was the title of the song. Now I do say Ballie, Ballie, Ballie, Ballie, Wallie. But that's when she walks right in and she walks right out. That's the title of the song. Sometimes I'll be singing the song. She…
Well I think the Atlantic record, the reissue, has Ball of the Wall on it. It's, uh, we're going to have a little fun with you all. Oh, yeah.
